jp: 我[わ]が家[や]には小[ちい]さな決[き]まりがあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、夕飯[ゆうはん]の前[まえ]にテレビを消[け]します。
en: Our family has a few small rules. For example, we turn off the TV before dinner.
why: The second sentence gives a concrete instance of the rules, so 例えば introduces the example.

jp: 朝[あさ]は家事[かじ]がたくさんあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、洗濯[せんたく]や掃除[そうじ]です。
en: There is a lot of housework in the morning. For example, laundry and cleaning.
why: Laundry and cleaning are named as examples of the housework, which calls for 例えば.

jp: 母[はは]は忙[いそが]しいのに、いつも工夫[くふう]しています。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、お弁当[べんとう]のおかずを毎日[まいにち]変[か]えています。
en: My mother is busy, but she always makes an effort. For example, she changes the side dishes in the lunch box every day.
why: A specific instance of her effort follows, so 例えば fits; a conclusion or contrast would not.

jp: 夜[よる]、寝[ね]る前[まえ]にすることがいくつかあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、歯[は]をみがいたり、日記[にっき]を書[か]いたりします。
en: There are a few things I do before going to bed. For example, I brush my teeth and write in my diary.
why: The second sentence lists samples of those things, which is what 例えば introduces.

jp: 私[わたし]の弟[おとうと]は習[なら]いごとをたくさんしています。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、水泳[すいえい]とピアノです。
en: My younger brother takes many lessons. For example, swimming and piano.
why: Swimming and piano are examples of the lessons, so 例えば introduces them.

jp: 家[いえ]の中[なか]には、電気[でんき]を使[つか]うものがたくさんあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]や洗濯機[せんたくき]です。
en: There are many things in a house that use electricity. For example, the refrigerator and the washing machine.
why: Appliances are given as examples of electric things, so 例えば is the right opener.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は毎日[まいにち]健康[けんこう]のために努力[どりょく]しています。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、朝[あさ]の散歩[さんぽ]を欠[か]かしません。
en: My grandfather makes an effort for his health every day. For example, he never skips his morning walk.
why: The morning walk is one concrete case of his effort, so 例えば is needed.

jp: 通勤[つうきん]の時間[じかん]を上手[じょうず]に使[つか]う人[ひと]もいます。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、電車[でんしゃ]の中[なか]で語学[ごがく]を勉強[べんきょう]します。
en: Some people make good use of their commuting time. For example, they study a language on the train.
why: Studying on the train is an example of using commuting time well, which 例えば marks.

jp: 節約[せつやく]のためにしていることがあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、買[か]い物[もの]の前[まえ]に冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]の中[なか]を確[たし]かめます。
en: There are things I do to save money. For example, I check the refrigerator before shopping.
why: Checking the fridge is one example of saving money, so 例えば opens the second sentence.

jp: 朝[あさ]の準備[じゅんび]が早[はや]く終[お]わるように、前[まえ]の晩[ばん]にしておくことがあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、服[ふく]を出[だ]しておきます。
en: I sometimes do things the night before so that I can get ready quickly in the morning. For example, I lay out my clothes.
why: Laying out clothes is a sample of what is done the night before, so 例えば is right.

jp: 子[こ]どもができる手伝[てつだ]いにはいろいろあります。{例[たと]えば|cn-tatoeba}、食器[しょっき]を運[はこ]んだり、ごみを出[だ]したりします。
en: There are various chores a child can help with. For example, carrying dishes or taking out the rubbish.
why: Carrying dishes and taking out rubbish are examples of chores, which 例えば introduces.

jp: うちの家族[かぞく]はみんな朝[あさ]が苦手[にがて]です。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、父[ちち]は起[お]きるのがとても遅[おそ]いです。
en: All of us in my family are bad at mornings. My father in particular is very slow to get up.
why: The father is singled out from 'everyone' for emphasis, which 特に or とりわけ expresses.

jp: 最近[さいきん]、家[いえ]の中[なか]が寒[さむ]いです。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、朝[あさ]の台所[だいどころ]は冷[ひ]えます。
en: It has been cold in the house lately. The kitchen in the morning especially gets chilly.
why: The kitchen in the morning is the most extreme case of the cold, so 特に/とりわけ highlights it.

jp: 私[わたし]は家[いえ]の掃除[そうじ]が好[す]きです。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、窓[まど]をきれいにするのが好[す]きです。
en: I like cleaning the house. I especially like making the windows spotless.
why: Window cleaning is the part the speaker likes most, so the emphasis word 特に/とりわけ is needed.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は甘[あま]いものが好[す]きです。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、チョコレートケーキには目[め]がありません。
en: My little sister likes sweet things. Chocolate cake in particular is her weakness.
why: Chocolate cake is highlighted as the strongest case of her liking sweets, so 特に/とりわけ fits.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]の食事[しょくじ]では野菜[やさい]を多[おお]く取[と]るようにしています。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、緑[みどり]の野菜[やさい]を心[こころ]がけています。
en: I try to eat plenty of vegetables at every meal. I particularly make a point of eating green vegetables.
why: Green vegetables are stressed within the general habit, which 特に/とりわけ marks.

jp: 今週[こんしゅう]は雨[あめ]が続[つづ]いて、洗濯物[せんたくもの]が乾[かわ]きません。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、タオルが乾[かわ]きにくくて困[こま]っています。
en: It has rained all week and the laundry won't dry. Towels in particular are hard to dry, which is a problem.
why: Towels are the worst case of the general problem, so the emphasis word 特に/とりわけ is used.

jp: 夏[なつ]の夜[よる]は暑[あつ]くて眠[ねむ]れません。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、エアコンのない二階[にかい]の部屋[へや]はひどいです。
en: Summer nights are too hot to sleep. The second-floor room without air conditioning is especially bad.
why: The room without air conditioning is singled out as the worst, so 特に/とりわけ is right.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]の作[つく]る料理[りょうり]はどれも懐[なつ]かしい味[あじ]です。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、煮物[にもの]は子[こ]どものころからの好物[こうぶつ]です。
en: Everything my grandmother cooks has a nostalgic taste. Her simmered dishes in particular have been my favourite since childhood.
why: Simmered dishes are picked out as the best among all her cooking, so 特に/とりわけ fits.

jp: 朝[あさ]の通勤[つうきん]ラッシュは、どの駅[えき]も混[こ]んでいます。{特[とく]に/とりわけ|cn-tatoeba}、月曜日[げつようび]の朝[あさ]はひどいです。
en: Every station is crowded during the morning rush. Monday mornings in particular are terrible.
why: Monday morning is the extreme case within the general crowding, so 特に/とりわけ is used.
